What it does

The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

Florida Senate - 2026 (NP) SR 1816 
 
 
 
 By Senator Burgess
 
 
 
 
 
 23-02646-26 20261816__
 1 Senate Resolution 
 2 A resolution recognizing CyberBay as a designated
 3 cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation
 4 region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledging
 5 Florida’s national leadership in cybersecurity
 6 readiness and digital defense, and affirming the
 7 importance of coordinated public-private partnerships
 8 to protect this state’s economic and digital security.
 9 
 10 WHEREAS, Florida is nationally recognized as a leader in
 11 cybersecurity preparedness, resilience, and digital defense,
 12 committed to strengthening its ability to protect government,
 13 industry, and citizens from evolving cyber threats, and
 14 WHEREAS, the Tampa Bay region is home to one of the
 15 nation’s most significant concentrations of military, defense,
 16 intelligence, and security operations, anchored by MacDill Air
 17 Force Base, a cornerstone of United States digital and national
 18 defense, and
 19 WHEREAS, this unique concentration of military assets,
 20 government institutions, research universities, and private
 21 sector technology companies has established Tampa Bay as a
 22 nationally recognized center of excellence for cybersecurity,
 23 technology innovation, and digital defense, and
 24 WHEREAS, this convergence has given rise to CyberBay, a
 25 cybersecurity and artificial intelligence ecosystem centered in
 26 the Tampa Bay area and built upon collaboration among the
 27 military, government, academia, and the private sector, and
 28 WHEREAS, CyberBay represents a coordinated regional
 29 initiative to advance cybersecurity readiness, artificial
 30 intelligence innovation, workforce development, and the defense
 31 of the United States’ digital infrastructure, and
 32 WHEREAS, the University of South Florida serves as a
 33 central anchor institution within CyberBay, including through
 34 the establishment of the Bellini College of Artificial
 35 Intelligence, Cybersecurity and Computing, one of the nation’s
 36 first colleges dedicated to the integrated study of these
 37 disciplines, and
 38 WHEREAS, the Bellini College of Artificial Intelligence,
 39 Cybersecurity and Computing plays a critical role in educating
 40 and preparing the next generation of cybersecurity and
 41 artificial intelligence professionals through degree programs,
 42 applied research, industry partnerships, internships, and
 43 experiential learning aligned with national and state workforce
 44 needs, and
 45 WHEREAS, the University of South Florida has articulated a
 46 mission to support cybersecurity readiness across Florida,
 47 including the long-term objective of extending cybersecurity
 48 services, expertise, and workforce support to municipalities
 49 throughout this state, and
 50 WHEREAS, CyberBay is further strengthened through strategic
 51 collaboration with Cyber Florida, this state’s designated
 52 cybersecurity planning and coordination organization, which
 53 advances statewide cyber resilience, workforce development,
 54 applied research, and public-private partnerships, and
 55 WHEREAS, CyberBay serves as a convening platform for
 56 collaboration and innovation, including through the CyberBay
 57 Conference, which brings together leaders from the technology,
 58 academic, government, and military sectors to address emerging
 59 cyber threats, workforce challenges, and technological
 60 advancements, and
 61 WHEREAS, public-private initiatives associated with
 62 CyberBay have supported cybersecurity improvements within
 63 regional municipalities, including the Cities of Tampa, St.
 64 Petersburg, and Clearwater, strengthening cyber readiness at the
 65 local level, and
 66 WHEREAS, private individuals have played a catalytic role
 67 in establishing and advancing the CyberBay ecosystem, including
 68 Lauren and Arnie Bellini, who have contributed and pledged more
 69 than $55 million to the University of South Florida to support
 70 education, research, workforce development, and the completion
 71 of a fully integrated cybersecurity and artificial intelligence
 72 ecosystem, and
 73 WHEREAS, such private investment was made with the stated
 74 objective of helping create and sustain up to 70,000 high
 75 paying, high-technology jobs in the Tampa Bay region by
 76 leveraging Florida’s existing strengths in national defense,
 77 cybersecurity, and innovation, and
 78 WHEREAS, CyberBay supports Florida’s economic
 79 competitiveness by attracting high-value employers, retaining
 80 talent within this state, strengthening workforce pipelines, and
 81 reinforcing this state’s leadership in cybersecurity, artificial
 82 intelligence, and digital defense, and
 83 WHEREAS, this state has a compelling interest in protecting
 84 its digital infrastructure, securing its economic future, and
 85 defending against rapidly evolving cyber threats that affect the
 86 government, industry, and citizens alike, NOW, THEREFORE,
 87 
 88 Be It Resolved by the Senate of the State of Florida:
 89 
 90 That the Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a
 91 cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region
 92 within the Tampa Bay area.
 93 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Legislature acknowledges
 94 Florida’s national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and
 95 recognizes CyberBay’s role in advancing statewide cybersecurity
 96 readiness and digital defense.
 97 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Legislature acknowledges
 98 the collaborative roles of the University of South Florida, the
 99 Bellini College of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity and
 100 Computing, Cyber Florida, municipal partners, and private sector
 101 stakeholders in advancing workforce development, technological
 102 innovation, and cybersecurity resilience.
 103 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Legislature affirms the
 104 importance of continued public-private collaboration to
 105 strengthen Florida’s cyber readiness, economic resilience, and
 106 leadership in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.
